sections.title: F1 — Major: a revoked domain can be cached again before its transaction commits
sections.text:
Owner: P07.1/P07.2. Confidence: high; source-proven concurrent schedule, not an additional database test execution.

Location: `packages/tenancy/src/Laravel/Support/HostResolverCacheInvalidator.php:36` and `:74–77`; registration in `packages/tenancy/src/Laravel/EventsRegistrar.php:44–45`.

`domainChanged()` immediately forgets the host cache on `eloquent.saved`/`eloquent.deleting`. These events run inside the writing transaction. `DomainTrustStateWriter::revoke()` changes `verified_at` and saves inside its transaction (`packages/tenancy/src/DomainTrust/Internal/DomainTrustStateWriter.php:109–134`). No after-commit host-cache invalidation is registered: `DomainTrustChanged` is dispatched after commit (`:193–197`), but no listener invalidates `HostAccountResolver` for that event. The resolver accepts a cached account id without checking domain trust (`packages/tenancy/src/Runtime/Internal/HostAccountResolver.php:29–43`).

Reproduction schedule with host caching enabled and a shared host store:

1. Verified `h.example.test` belongs to active account A. Prime its host-cache entry.
2. Writer W begins revocation, sets `verified_at = NULL`, and calls `Domain::save()`. The saved listener forgets the host-cache entry while W's transaction is still open.
3. Before W commits, reader R resolves that host on another connection. PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED exposes the previously committed verified row. `lookup()` returns A and `resolve()` puts A into the shared cache (`HostAccountResolver.php:35–39,62–70`).
4. W commits. Its after-commit domain event does not clear the newly populated entry.
5. The next HTTP request for the revoked host gets cached A. `ResolveTenantFromHost.php:47–56` loads the still-active account and initializes A, instead of rejecting the now-unverified host. The stale entry survives up to `host_identification.cache_ttl` (default 300 seconds).

The same window exists for transactional domain deletion/reassignment. This defeats the verified-host entry boundary in D95 §6 and the resolver's own documented predicate. It needs neither a broken cache backend nor an external SQL bypass.

Existing coverage: `HostResolutionTest.php:200` changes a domain and checks the next resolution serially, after the save. It does not interleave another reader before commit. `DomainTrustTest` exercises transactionality, but not concurrent refill of the new host resolver cache.

Repair direction: invalidate captured normalized old/current host keys after successful commit as well, and ensure an in-flight cache miss cannot publish a pre-revocation mapping after that invalidation. Add a two-connection/shared-cache regression for revoke and reassignment. Keep fail-closed trust semantics; repair belongs to the engine/model owning item, not P07.6.

sections.title: F2 — Minor: the specified native-permission validation command selects no tests
sections.text:
Owner: P07.4 validation carrier / P07.6 contract. Confidence: reproduced.

Location: `@plan/phases/P07/P07.6.json:26`; `packages/access/composer.json` script `test`; `packages/access/tests/Pg/NativePermissionTest.php:24`.

The contract calls `scripts/php84 composer --working-dir=packages/access test -- --filter=NativePermission`. The package's `test` script adds `--exclude-group=pg`, while every NativePermission test belongs to `pg`. Exact command output is `No tests found`, exit 1. It cannot provide the required GREEN result on this candidate.

The bounded corrected carrier `PGSQL_PORT=5434 scripts/php84 composer --working-dir=packages/access test:pg -- --filter=NativePermission` passed 5 tests / 20 assertions. Native permission behavior is not red on that evidence; the written acceptance command is wrong. Update the owning carrier to `test:pg` and keep the exact original failure in its evidence. No contract was edited during this review.

sections.title: Owner-authorized corrections (execution, no new review)
sections.text:
Owner instructions: «я же написал с автоисправлениями»; «ревью не делай, только исправления». The owner's prior instruction permits manual plan correction when the skm rewrite causes errors. The original findings/range above remain historical evidence; no second verdict or reviewer was produced.

Product correction commit: `32e1817c74abcd59d5a29b51c384c7cb93f89aaa`. F1 owning correction is in P07.1/P07.2 code, with unchanged public constructor/method signatures. Host cache entries carry a random shared generation. Successful commit advances the generation; a delayed cache publication retains its older generation and cannot authorize this or subsequent requests. Transactions bypass shared reads/writes. Saved/deleted events cover completed SQL and account deletion cascades. In-transaction invalidation proves cache writability while domain verification can still roll back; commit advances the fence again. The lifecycle's physical entry removal after commit is retained. A missing/evicted generation is freshly initialized, preventing reuse of old entries.

Tradeoff: account/domain mutations invalidate all warmed host mappings, rebuilt on demand. Stable cache hits retain zero central SQL queries. Public SPI signatures, migrations and API manifests are unchanged. Package README/CHANGELOG document the behavior.

F2 owning carrier now uses `PGSQL_PORT=5434 scripts/php84 composer --working-dir=packages/access test:pg -- --filter=NativePermission` in P07.6.md. The original no-tests failure remains recorded above.

New regressions use two independent PostgreSQL connections to `corex_test` and one real file-backed host cache outside tenant stores. A one-shot framework WritingKey listener deterministically commits between SQL lookup and cache publication. The eight principal regressions fail on the prior product: revoke, rename, reassignment, domain deletion, account pending-shell transition, account cascade deletion, delayed publication and rolled-back verification. Additional cases cover warmed-cache transaction bypass and generation eviction. No sleeps or external services are required. Fixtures create tenant databases with `_test` suffix and clean them afterward.
